notes: Mark FC when multiple pops occur close together; hold settings. Don't increase heat to chase a brief FC dip.

history.change: Initial procedure, copied from Colombian Supremo: charge burner 55 / SV 230; burner 45 at 154, 40 + air 40 at 175, 35 at 178, 30 at 190, 25 at 194, 15 at 198. Drops lowered from the Supremo's: espresso 206.0 (Supremo 207.4), pourover 203.5 (Supremo 204.3). References are Supremo #30 (espresso) and #40 (pourover); there is no roast of this bean yet.
history.why: Untried bean, so this starts from the most similar one with history: Colombian Supremo, our most-roasted Colombian washed coffee. Sweet Maria's Colombia Productores de Buesaco: a small-producer blend from farms around Buesaco, Narino; washed Bourbon, Caturra, Typica types and modern hybrids; total score 87.8; City to Full City+. Toffee and creamy caramel, milk chocolate, baked apple and pear butter as it cools, juicy acidity. The steps stay the Supremo's; Narino coffee is typically grown very high (often 1,800 m and up), so it may be denser than the Supremo and reach FC a little later: watch whether FC lands later than the Supremo's ~7:00-7:15. The drops come down because this lot's appeal is its fruit and caramel, which a lighter roast keeps: espresso 1.4 under the Supremo's, toward Full City rather than Full City+, and pourover 0.8 under, toward City+. Both are first guesses; adjust after tasting.
